From: Claire Zhou <claire@emberhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pricing request — vendor match / migration credit

Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week. EmberHealth is close to a procurement decision but we have a competing offer from a vendor who is offering a cheaper line-item for the A100 pool we're currently evaluating. Two asks from procurement:

1) Can Redwood provide a SKU swap option so the commit uses a denser GPU SKU (NVIDIA B200 equivalent) for the same anticipated throughput rather than the A100 SKU? They want to optimize for sustained throughput rather than peak tokens.

2) Would Redwood consider a one-time migration credit to offset migration and validation costs? Our procurement lead has penciled in a $60k sensitivity.

If you can get us a short-term discount or migration credit, EmberHealth can sign a 12-month reserved commit by end of month. I can loop procurement.

Appreciate a fast reply — procurement deadline is 4/30.

Claire
Claire Zhou
Head of Platform Partnerships
EmberHealth

Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated pricing request — vendor match / migration credit

Jonas / Laura — reviewed Ember's usage profile. Short summary: they need sustained throughput of ~1200 tokens/sec across a mixed workload (chat + streaming gen) with a 95th percentile latency SLO of 250ms. Two technical options:

- Keep A100 SKU and tune batching + caching to hit throughput (higher $/GPU, easier compatibility).
- Swap to denser B200-equivalent SKU: fewer cards, better sustained throughput per card, slightly higher ops per dollar for long sequences but lower latency predictability for microbursts.

Financially (ballpark): swapping to the B200 SKU reduces Redwood unit revenue by ~12% compared to A100 baseline on the same committed $ value. We can offset with a small uplift to the monthly commit or offer a one-time migration credit.

Proposed commercial response (draft):
- One-time migration credit: $50,000 (covers validation + migration of models and KV cache seeding).
- 3-month ramp discount: 20% off committed rate for months 1-3, then full committed rate for remainder of 12 months.
- Throughput guarantee: we can offer an operational target (95th pctl) with credits tied to missing the target for sustained 1-hour windows (ceded back via usage credit up to 10% of monthly commit). Legal to confirm exact SLA phrasing.

I'm attaching an updated pricing-sheet (pricing-sheet-v3.xlsx) with modeled lanes. If this is acceptable I can present to Ember procurement with the SOW draft.

-Marissa

Attachments: pricing-sheet-v3.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Subject: Request for exec approval: EmberHealth SKU swap + $50k credit

Vivek — quick ask. EmberHealth (EMB-4782) is asking for a SKU swap to a denser GPU family plus a one-time migration credit. Marissa ran numbers and proposes $50k credit + 3-month 20% ramp. We would lose ~12% unit revenue vs A100 baseline if we accept the swap, but the commit is a 12-month reserved deal with decent ARR and low churn risk (enterprise healthcare account).

Key points:
- Revenue: projected ARR (net of credit amortized) remains positive and covers COGS + target margin assuming 70% utilization.
- Competitive motion: incumbent is offering a lower headline SKU price; this concession is strategic to prevent them from going to competitor.
- Risk: throughput SLA needs precise legal language; Laura flagged a 30-day remediation period and operational playbook requirement.

Asking for explicit approval to offer: $50k one-time credit, 20% discount for months 1-3, and the SKU swap with a conditional SLA credit cap of 10% MRC. Customer signs 12-month reserved commit.

If approved, I'll send the packaged SOW + DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Jonas

- One-time migration credit: $50,000 (applied as an MRC credit over the first two invoices).
- Billing: 12-month reserved commit (final committed $ to be reflected in SOW).
- Ramp: 20% off committed rate for months 1-3. Months 4-12 will include a 5% uplift to protect margin (per approved exec direction).
- SKU swap: approved to move the commit to the denser B200-equivalent SKU with the understanding that throughput guarantees will be operationalized via an SLA addendum.
- SLA: Redwood will provide a 95th percentile throughput target; credits for missed targets capped at 10% of monthly commit and subject to a 30-day remediation clause.

Next steps for Ember: review SOW, sign DocuSign. For Redwood: CS will own migration plan and runbooks; legal will finalize SLA language. We can schedule a migration kickoff next week if you sign.

Thanks — excited to partner on this.
